chunks: And among what was narrated by Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Fuḍayl Sukkarah, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, is there a fixed limit for water? He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: When I die, draw for me six water-skins from the well of Ghars, then wash me and shroud me. So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report, because they are to be understood as pertaining to a kind of recommendation. For the merit in washing the deceased is that abundant and ample water be used, and the water should not be restricted therein, although if one were to suffice with the amount that purifies him, whatever is encompassed by the name of ghusl (ritual washing) would be sufficient.

key_terms.اسْمُ الْغُسْلِ: that which legally counts as ghusl (ritual washing)
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, indicating a preferred but non-obligatory practice
key_terms.بِئْرِ غَرْسٍ: the well of Ghars from which water was drawn
key_terms.سِتَّ قِرَبٍ: six water-skins used for drawing water
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْنِي: then wash me, referring to the deceased's ghusl (ritual washing)
key_terms.وَكَفِّنِّي: and shroud me in a kafan

ai.seo_question: Is there a fixed amount of water required for washing the deceased in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the amount of water used in washing the deceased. It indicates that using abundant water is recommended and more virtuous, while the minimum amount that fulfills the act of ghusl (ritual washing) is still sufficient.
